Let \(x_*=0\) and \(f_*=0\), after translating. Write

\[
f_i=f(x_i),\qquad g_i=\nabla f(x_i),\qquad a_i=\|g_i\|^2 \quad (i=0,1,2).
\]

Because the searches are exact, the gradients are orthogonal to the searched spaces:

\[
g_1\perp g_0,\qquad g_2\perp g_0,\qquad g_2\perp g_1.
\]

Also \(x_i-x_0\in \operatorname{span}\{g_0,\dots,g_{i-1}\}\), so

\[
\langle g_i,x_0\rangle=\langle g_i,x_i\rangle .
\]

For every convex \(1\)-smooth \(f\),

\[
0=f_*\ge f_i+\langle g_i,-x_i\rangle+\frac12\|g_i\|^2,
\]

hence

\[
\langle g_i,x_0\rangle=\langle g_i,x_i\rangle\ge f_i+\frac12 a_i.
\]

Since \(g_0,g_1,g_2\) are mutually orthogonal,

\[
1\ge \|x_0\|^2
\ge \sum_{i=0}^2 \frac{\langle g_i,x_0\rangle^2}{\|g_i\|^2}
\ge \sum_{i=0}^2 \frac{(f_i+a_i/2)^2}{a_i}.
\]

Next, for \(i<j\), smooth convexity gives

\[
f_i\ge f_j+\langle g_j,x_i-x_j\rangle+\frac12\|g_i-g_j\|^2.
\]

The inner product vanishes by exactness, so

\[
a_i+a_j\le 2(f_i-f_j).
\]

Let \(s=f_2\). Scaling by \(s\), the sharp minimization of the right-hand side above is attained when

\[
a_2=2s,\qquad a_1=\frac{2s}{\sqrt5},\qquad a_0=2s+\frac{2s}{\sqrt5},
\]

with

\[
f_1=s\left(2+\frac1{\sqrt5}\right),\qquad
f_0=s\left(3+\frac3{\sqrt5}\right).
\]

Substitution gives

\[
1\ge s(14+4\sqrt5).
\]

Therefore

\[
f(x_2)-f_*\le \frac1{14+4\sqrt5}.
\]

This bound is sharp: the equality data above satisfy the finite smooth-convex interpolation inequalities, so they are realized by a differentiable convex \(1\)-smooth function in \(\mathbb R^3\). Scaling the realizing construction so that \(\|x_0-x_*\|=1\) gives equality.

Thus

\[
\boxed{W_2=\frac1{14+4\sqrt5}}
\]

equivalently \(W_2=\dfrac{7-2\sqrt5}{58}\).
